incidente.resumo: A bug in third-party datacenter control system logic made the cooling control system unresponsive during a control-host failover; in a small portion of one Tokyo Availability Zone cooling shut down and EC2 servers powered off from overheating, impairing EC2 instances and EBS volumes. Operators manually reset equipment and unresponsive PLCs to restore cooling, after which power was restored and most instances recovered.

descricao.texto: Beginning at 12:36 PM JST, a small percentage of EC2 servers in a single Availability Zone of the Tokyo Region shut down due to overheating; the text does not say how this was noticed.
trechos: Beginning at 12:36 PM JST, a small percentage of EC2 servers in a single Availability Zone in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region shut down due to overheating.

gatilho.texto: Just prior to the event, the datacenter control system was in the process of failing away from one of the control hosts.
trechos: Just prior to the event, the datacenter control system was in the process of failing away from one of the control hosts.

descricao.texto: During the failover, the control system exchanges information with other control systems and datacenter equipment; due to a bug in the third-party control system logic, this exchange resulted in excessive interactions between the control system and the devices, which ultimately made the control system unresponsive.
trechos: During this kind of failover, the control system has to exchange information with other control systems and the datacenter equipment it controls (e.g., the cooling equipment and temperature sensors throughout the datacenter) to ensure that the new control host has the most up-to-date information about the state of the datacenter.

Due to a bug in the third-party control system logic, this exchange resulted in excessive interactions between the control system and the devices in the datacenter which ultimately resulted in the control system becoming unresponsive.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The cooling systems are designed to go into maximum cooling mode if the control system fails; this worked in most of the datacenter, but in a small portion the cooling system did not transition to this safe configuration and instead shut down.
trechos: Our datacenters are designed such that if the datacenter control system fails, the cooling systems go into maximum cooling mode until the control system functionality is restored.
While this worked correctly in most of the datacenter, in a small portion of the datacenter, the cooling system did not correctly transition to this safe cooling configuration and instead shut down.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The PLCs controlling some of the air handling units were also unresponsive; their failure prevented the default cooling and the operator-initiated purge mode from working.
trechos: During this process, it was discovered that the PLCs controlling some of the air handling units were also unresponsive.
It was the failure of these PLC controllers which prevented the default cooling and “purge” mode from correctly working.
The team attempted to activate purge in the affected areas of the datacenter, but this also failed.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Because the datacenter control system was unavailable, the operations team had minimum visibility into the health and state of the cooling systems.
trechos: Because the datacenter control system was unavailable, the operations team had minimum visibility into the health and state of the datacenter cooling systems.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Some instances and volumes were on hardware adversely affected by the loss of power and excessive heat; they took longer to recover and some had to be retired due to underlying hardware failures.
trechos: A small number of instances and volumes were hosted on hardware which was adversely affected by the loss of power and excessive heat.
It took longer to recover these instances and volumes and some needed to be retired as a result of failures to the underlying hardware.

passos.texto: The team attempted to bypass the control systems and activate purge mode in the affected areas, but this also failed.
trechos: As an added safeguard, our datacenter operators have the ability to bypass the datacenter control systems and put our cooling system in “purge” mode to quickly exhaust hot air in the event of a malfunction.
The team attempted to activate purge in the affected areas of the datacenter, but this also failed.

passos.texto: To recover, the team had to manually investigate and reset all of the affected pieces of equipment and put them into a maximum cooling configuration.
trechos: To recover, the team had to manually investigate and reset all of the affected pieces of equipment and put them into a maximum cooling configuration.

passos.texto: At 2:51 PM JST engineers resolved the issue affecting the RunInstances idempotency token and Auto Scaling.
trechos: At 2:51 PM JST, engineers resolved the issue affecting the “idempotency token” and Auto Scaling.

passos.texto: The unresponsive PLCs controlling some air handling units were reset; after that, cooling was restored to the affected area (at 3:21 PM JST) and temperatures began to decrease.
trechos: During this process, it was discovered that the PLCs controlling some of the air handling units were also unresponsive. These controllers needed to be reset.
After these controllers were reset, cooling was restored to the affected area of the datacenter and temperatures began to decrease.
The affected cooling systems were restored at 3:21 PM JST and temperatures in the affected areas began to return to normal.

passos.texto: As temperatures returned to normal, power was restored to the affected instances; the EC2 control plane subsystem was restored in the impacted AZ at 4:05 PM JST, and by 6:30 PM JST the vast majority of affected instances and volumes had recovered.
trechos: As temperatures returned to normal, power was restored to the affected instances.
Launches of new EC2 instances in the affected Availability Zone continued to fail until 4:05 PM JST, when the EC2 control plane subsystem had been restored in the impacted Availability Zone.
By 6:30 PM JST, the vast majority of affected instances and volumes had recovered.

acoes.texto: Already done: the failover mode that triggered the bug was disabled on the control systems.
trechos: In the interim, we have disabled the failover mode that triggered this bug on our control systems to ensure we do not have a recurrence of this issue.

acoes.texto: Already done: local operations teams were trained to quickly identify and remediate this situation if it recurs.
trechos: We have also trained our local operations teams to quickly identify and remediate this situation if it were to recur, and we are confident that we could reset the system before seeing any customer impact if a similar situation was to occur for any reason.

acoes.texto: Modify the way the impacted air handling units are controlled so that purge mode can bypass the PLC controllers completely, an approach already used in the newest datacenter designs.
trechos: Finally, we are working to modify the way that we control the impacted air handling units to ensure that “purge mode” is able to bypass the PLC controllers completely.
This is an approach we have begun using in our newest datacenter designs and will make us even more confident that “purge mode” will work even if PLCs become unresponsive.

acoes.texto: Recommendation to customers: for the highest availability, run applications across multiple Availability Zones.
trechos: For customers that need the highest availability for their applications, we continue to recommend running applications with this multiple Availability Zone architecture; any application component that can create availability issues for customers should run in this fault tolerant way.
Beginning at 12:36 PM JST, a small percentage of EC2 servers in a single Availability Zone in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region shut down due to overheating.
By 6:30 PM JST, the vast majority of affected instances and volumes had recovered.

perguntas_em_aberto: The vendors and the company are still working to understand the bug, and the subsequent interactions, that caused both the control system and the impacted PLCs to become unresponsive.

observacoes: Domain classified as infra_fisica_datacenter because the bug is in the third-party control software of the datacenter cooling system, by analogy with the prompt's rule that embedded software in physical systems keeps the physical system's domain. Duration computed from 12:36 PM JST (servers began shutting down) to 6:30 PM JST (vast majority of instances and volumes recovered); a small number of instances on damaged hardware took longer and some were retired. The text also mentions isolated cross-AZ impact for some customers using Application Load Balancer with AWS WAF or sticky sessions, with details shared only directly with those customers.
